finding_key: packages/backend/src/auth/github.strategy.ts::the browser (non-cli) github oauth flow sends no `state` parameter at all, so it has no csrf protection — contradicting the risk-table row this diff's rest-api.md edit sits next to
evidence: Verified against the supplied sources: github.strategy.ts:43-49 passes no `state: true`/store to passport-oauth2, and authenticate() (lines ~57-64) sets `opts.state` only when `req.__cliStateToken` exists; github-auth.guard.ts sets that token only for `mode === 'cli'` (its own test asserts the web flow gets no state and no `createState` call). So the browser OAuth flow sends and verifies no state, leaving it open to login CSRF, while the rest-api.md risk-table row edited in this diff claims per-request CSRF tokens are validated on callback — true only of the CLI branch. Confidence is medium rather than high because the full web branch of githubAuthCallback was not supplied and I relied on standard passport-oauth2 null-state-store semantics; the defect is also pre-existing, which the claim acknowledges.
